document_summary: Article II (General Regulations) of Chapter 155, Rent Control, of the City of Hoboken, NJ Code, covering base rent control, the annual cost-of-living cap, and tax, capital-improvement and hardship surcharges.

rules.title: Hoboken Rent Control: cost-of-living increase cap (Code § 155-5)
rules.requirement: At lease expiration or periodic-tenancy termination, a landlord may not demand or receive an increase above the lesser of 5% or the CPI percentage change. Only one such cost-of-living increase is allowed in any twelve-month period, regardless of how many tenants occupy the unit.
rules.key_value: Lesser of 5% or CPI change; one increase per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing space in dwellings to which Chapter 155 applies (applicability and exemptions are defined elsewhere in the chapter, not in this capture). Rents are controlled at the base rent received as of October 1, 1985 (§ 155-4).
rules.interaction: City rent control ordinance. Surcharges for taxes, water/sewer and capital improvements are not rent for computing cost-of-living increases. A capital improvement surcharge may not raise base rents by more than 33 1/3% in any 12 months (§ 155-10). Hardship increases require Board approval (§ 155-14).
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.
rules.extraction_notes: Section 155-5 is marked 'Amended 2-1-2023 by Ord. No. B-532'. Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication). The pre-2023 text and original cap are not shown, so it is unclear whether the 2023 amendment changed the 5%/CPI value. § 155-4 (amended through Ord. B-818, 10-22-2025) requires 30 days' written notice with reasons for any increase.  A disclosure statement and a two-year limitation on refunds also apply.  This document does not cover vacancy decontrol or applicability.  It also does not mention the NJ FAIR Act.  Tax, water/sewer, capital and hardship surcharges are addressed in §§ 155-6 to 155-14.  Those are folded into this record.  They do not create separate records.  No other category is addressed in this document.  The 33 1/3% cap is noted under interaction.  It is not a separate headline value.  The Article's other sections are procedural.  The Board's review timing is in § 155-17.  Nothing else here changes the headline cap.
